descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-94659 AC 2, AC 4-9 · “Real OTP delivery is confirmed on a live production login attempt, including to a Gmail and an Outlook address”.

Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S01 A real code email on dev (TFA-94659 AC 1-3) and on production to Gmail and Outlook (AC 4-9)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T7 On the dev deployment, a live login attempt delivers a real OTP email (not a simulated or logged one), so email-code sign-in can be tested end to end. (TFA-94659 AC 1; TFA-94659 AC 2; TFA-94659 AC 3)
  • T8 Production: SES is configured on the production deployment, the AWS account is out of SES sandbox, and the sending domain is verified with SPF, DKIM and DMARC. (TFA-94659 AC 4; TFA-94659 AC 5; TFA-94659 AC 6)
  • T9 The OTP email comes from a clear sender (e.g. no-reply@roundcompanion.com) with the sender name 'Round Companion'. It contains only the code and basic instructions, with no patient information. (TFA-94659 AC 7; TFA-94659 AC 8)
  • T10 Real OTP delivery is confirmed on a live production login, to a Gmail address and to an Outlook address. (TFA-94659 AC 9)

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given Run by a person, never the agent. Dev cell: only with Quinn's or Daniela's explicit OK for that run, a team-controlled mailbox that has never signed in, and never the store-review account or any review address. …

When In each cell: enter the address and press Send sign-in code; note the seconds until the email arrives (10 sends per mailbox); open the email and its headers; enter the code and press Sign in. On prod also open the SES account page (production access or sandbox) and the domain identity. …

Then Each email reaches the inbox (not spam, not a console or log line). The sender name is 'Round Companion' and the address is on the verified sending domain. The body holds only the code and basic instructions. On prod the headers show SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass for roundcompanion.com, and SES shows production access and a verified domain. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): T7 (AC 1-3): Pass only if a real email from dev reaches the inbox. T8 (AC 4-6): SES production access, a verified domain, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass in the headers. T9 (AC 7-8): the sender name is exactly 'Round Companion' and the address is on the verified sending domain (AC 7's no-reply@roundcompanion.com is an example, not the rule); …

Where it ran: dev; test method CONFIG · Config check; lane planned in the matrix: manual (blocked)

S01 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.
